abstract: Assesses telemetry bandwidth verification and substation recording buffer specifications
system_message:
You are the Operational technology network architect (NETW). Your responsibilities include assessing telemetry bandwidth verification and substation recording buffer specifications across the regional intertie blackout investigation corridor.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Substation optical fiber attenuation（OPTIC）
information_points.content:
NETW-OPTIC-F9S：According to the optical time-domain reflectometry report on substation perimeter optical ground wire links, the Substation Digital Fault Recorder Triangulation plan reflects an optical loss margin of 3.5 dB.
NETW-OPTIC-Y7O：According to the optical time-domain reflectometry report covering substation perimeter optical ground wire links, the High-Speed Event Sequence Waveform Reconstruction plan exhibits an optical loss margin of 4.2 dB.
NETW-OPTIC-GS0：According to the optical time-domain reflectometry report covering substation perimeter optical ground wire links, the Synchronized Phasor Dynamic Trajectory Analysis plan has an optical loss margin of 5.0 dB.

information_points.title: Assesses telemetry bandwidth verification and substation recording buffer specifications（OTNET）
information_points.content:
NETW-OTNET-HJQ：For the Synchronized Phasor Dynamic Trajectory Analysis plan, the wide-area network telemetry engineering review across the dedicated multiplexed packet network between substations and the primary control center confirmed that telemetry bandwidth capacity is certified (true). Additionally, the digital fault recorder technical specification sheet indicates a substation recording buffer interval of 10 ms for its local transient memory ring buffer.
NETW-OTNET-98B：For the Substation Digital Fault Recorder Triangulation plan, telemetry bandwidth capacity is certified (true) across the dedicated multiplexed packet network between substations and the primary control center based on the wide-area network telemetry engineering review, and the digital fault recorder technical specification sheet notes a substation recording buffer interval of 10 ms in its local transient memory ring buffer.
NETW-OTNET-I7O：For the High-Speed Event Sequence Waveform Reconstruction plan, the wide-area network telemetry engineering review indicates that telemetry bandwidth capacity is not certified (false) on the dedicated multiplexed packet network between substations and the primary control center, while the digital fault recorder technical specification sheet establishes a substation recording buffer interval of 20 ms for the local transient memory ring buffer.
